subject: Validation matrix & targeted test schedule
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Validation matrix & targeted test schedule

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed, pragmatic test plan so we can get to a like-for-like comparison in the bake-off. High-level pain points you confirmed:

- Unpredictable p95 latency under peak traffic (affecting clinical workflows)
- Cost volatility with current hosted inference provider
- Data residency and PHI-sensitive routing requirements
- Occasional model drift/hallucination on diagnosis-style prompts

Primary goals you shared:
- P95 latency under 200ms for typical 512-token prompts
- Predictable monthly unit cost within your current budget envelope (~$Xk/month)
- VPC/on-prem control for PHI workflows and audit logs for queries
- Maintain or improve model fidelity on 500 clinical QA prompts

Decision criteria (what Lumina will weigh):
1) Latency & stability (p95/p99 across simulated load)
2) Cost per 1k tokens and predictable billing
3) Security / compliance (SOC 2, VPC/KMS support)
4) Integration effort and engineering runbook
5) Observability (token-level tracing / per-request cost attribution)

Proposed targeted tests (we can prune based on what you want prioritized):
A) Baseline throughput test: 1M tokens/day traffic pattern to measure p50/p95/p99 and compute cost per token.
B) PHI/VPC validation: end-to-end ingress to a customer VPC (redwood private control plane) to verify routing and audit logs.
C) Regression fidelity: run your 500 clinical prompts and measure hallucination/regression against your current baseline.
D) Failover & routing: cross-region failover to verify graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.

Attachments: I uploaded a draft "validation_matrix.xlsx" (columns: criterion, test, metric, target, owner, timeframe) and the raw demo recording to the Drive link below.

Suggested next steps / timeline (provisional):
- Week of 5/3: confirm which of A-D are in scope and which tests Lumina wants prioritized
- By 5/9: Redwood runs baseline throughput test and shares logs + cost estimates
- 5/11: architecture deep-dive with your Infra team (30–45m) to plan VPC onboarding
- 5/18: run regression fidelity batch and share evaluation CSV

Owners on our side: Evelyn (commercial lead / timeline), Marissa (technical lead / tests), Karthik (pricing & commercial terms).

Can you confirm which tests you want as "must have" for vendor selection and whether procurement should be looped in now? Happy to rework the matrix to match your internal rubric.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@luminahealth.com>

Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 13:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Validation matrix & targeted test schedule

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear recap and the proposed matrix. This maps closely to what our stakeholders care about. A few quick answers and asks:

- "Must have" tests for our vendor selection: A (throughput baseline), B (PHI/VPC validation), and C (regression fidelity). D is nice-to-have but can be deprioritized if we need speed.
- Can you also provide a short SOC 2 summary and confirmation of KMS/HSM integrations for key material? I'll need that for our security team.
- Procurement is on copy — they asked for a ballpark monthly range for a Dedicated/reserved configuration that meets the baseline numbers in A. High level is fine for now (range and what drives the top/bottom).
- Two quick technical questions for Marissa/Karthik: 1) Do you expose token-level observability so our engineers can tie tokens back to UX flows? 2) Can we pin a model version (no automatic upgrades) during the POC?

If you can get the SOC 2 doc and a short plain-English test schedule (who does what and when) by EOD Monday (5/3), procurement and security can start their internal review.

Thanks —
Alyssa Cheng
Head of Integrations, LuminaHealth
alyssa@luminahealth.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Validation matrix & targeted test schedule

Alyssa —

Thanks — super helpful. Quick answers inline and an updated, concrete schedule below.

- SOC 2 / KMS: attaching a 1-pager "soc2-summary.pdf" that highlights scope and KMS integrations. We support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and HSM options for Private deployments.
- Token-level observability: yes — we expose per-request token counts, latency breakdowns, and a trace id you can push into your logging. We also include token-level cost attribution in our Console (can be exported to CSV).
- Model pinning: yes — you can pin a model version for the POC and we will not auto-upgrade that endpoint.

Updated plan (concrete owners & dates):
- 5/3: finalize scope (A, B, C) — Alyssa to confirm must-haves (you indicated A/B/C)
- 5/5: Redwood delivers a plain-English test schedule + validation_matrix.xlsx (attached) and ballpark Dedicated pricing range
- 5/9: baseline throughput run (Redwood) — deliver artifacts: load generator config, perf logs, and cost calc
- 5/11: Infra deep-dive (30m) with Lumina infra + Redwood infra (Marissa lead) — agenda: VPC peering/ingress, audit logs, KMS key handoff
- 5/14: SOC 2 artifact review (security) — deliver: soc2-summary.pdf + evidence pointers
- 5/18: regression fidelity batch (Lumina provides 500 prompts; Redwood returns evaluation CSV)

Owners: Evelyn (program lead), Marissa (technical owner for tests & infra), Karthik (pricing & SOW), Redwood infra on standby for the 5/11 call.

Pricing: Karthik — can you draft a short ballpark range (low / mid / high) for the Dedicated configuration that meets the baseline? I think Alyssa wants a high-level monthly range and what drives the delta.

Attaching: validation_matrix.xlsx (draft), soc2-summary.pdf, sample_kv_cache_test_plan.pdf (KV/cache test approach).

If that timeline looks good, I'll lock calendar invites and share the architecture agenda for 5/11.

—Evelyn
